findings.evidence: The form contains with no form action/target defined, and immediately below it a separate Continue. The destination screen (#invite-sent) states: "An invite was sent to the address entered above."
findings.fix: Make the single control that actually sends the invite unambiguous: either have Continue perform the submit and remove the redundant Save button, or have Save itself navigate to #invite-sent on success and remove Continue, and state that result explicitly.
findings.location: Invite a team member screen (#invite-member): the form's "Save" button and the separate "Continue" link
findings.violation: Two separate controls exist for what the copy implies is one action (sending the invite): a submit button whose outcome is nowhere specified, and a plain navigation link to a confirmation screen that asserts the invite was sent. The artifact never states that activating Continue is what triggers the send, nor what Save does if clicked instead. A user can reach the "Invite sent" confirmation without any specified send having occurred, or can click Save and see no result at all.

findings.evidence: <button id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" type="button" aria-label="Duplicate project"></button> has no href, no form association, and no visible text; no part of the artifact names what happens after it is activated, and no new/duplicated project appears anywhere in the artifact.
findings.fix: Define what activating Duplicate project does: the new project it creates, where it appears (e.g. in the projects list), and a visible confirmation that the duplication succeeded.
findings.violation: Duplicating a project changes stored state (it is expected to create a new project) but the artifact specifies absolutely no outcome: no in-progress indication, no success message, no new state, not even a defined target. A user who activates it has no way, now or ever within this spec, to tell whether anything happened.

findings.evidence: "'Vendor Onboarding' has been moved to archived projects. It no longer appears in the active projects list for anyone on the team." The only control on the screen is Back to your projects; no section, link, or control anywhere in the artifact names an unarchive, restore, or view-archived-projects action.
findings.fix: Add a stated restore/unarchive path, e.g. a link to an archived-projects view from which a project can be unarchived, and name it on the project-archived confirmation.
findings.violation: Archiving is a committed action on a project that is reasonably reversible in this kind of product (unlike a permanent delete), but the artifact names no reversal path anywhere: no unarchive control, no archived-projects list to act from. As specified, an accidental archive has no way back.

findings.evidence: "Import failed. Error code IMP-500. Contact support if this continues."
findings.fix: Replace the raw code with plain language naming what failed (e.g. which file or step) and why, reserving the code as supplementary detail rather than the explanation itself.
findings.violation: The message surfaces a raw internal error code (IMP-500) and names no action, field, or specific cause; it does not say what about the import failed (which file, which record, which validation), so the user cannot tell what went wrong or whether anything they did caused it.

findings.evidence: The only control on the screen is Back to your projects; the message says "Contact support if this continues" with no contact control, address, or link, and no retry control anywhere on the screen.
findings.fix: Add a retry control on the import status screen, and make "contact support" an actual reachable control (a link or address), both available where the error appears.
findings.violation: The error names two possible next steps in prose (retry implicitly, by "if this continues"; contact support explicitly) but provides a route for neither: there is no retry action and no reachable way to contact support from the error state itself.

findings.evidence: <button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button> and <button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>; neither form carries an action attribute, and neither section defines any success message, saved indicator, or transition after Save is activated.
findings.fix: Specify a visible save confirmation at each Save button (an inline success message, a saved-state indicator, or a defined next state), so the artifact commits to telling the user the save happened.
findings.location: Project settings screen (#project-settings) "Save" button, and Notifications screen (#notification-settings) "Save" button
findings.violation: Both Save actions change stored state but the artifact specifies no visible indication of what happened: no confirmation message, no changed control state, no next screen. The only feedback a user has is that the typed value remains in the field, which does not distinguish a successful save from the click having done nothing.

findings.evidence: Back to your projects sits beside an editable, unsaved "Project name" field; Back to project settings sits beside an unsaved "Digest frequency" select. Neither link's label, nor any other text on either screen, says what becomes of an edited-but-unsaved field.
findings.fix: Either warn before navigating away from an unsaved edit, or have the back link state (or the screen state) make clear that unsaved changes are discarded on leaving.

instances.location: Project settings screen (#project-settings), "Back to your projects" link (project-settings-back-link)
Notifications screen (#notification-settings), "Back to project settings" link (notification-settings-back-link)

findings.location: Project settings screen (#project-settings) "Back to your projects" link, and Notifications screen (#notification-settings) "Back to project settings" link
findings.violation: Both exits are reachable and predictably labeled as navigation, but neither the artifact nor the label discloses that taking them discards an in-progress, unsaved edit to the field on the same screen. A user who edits the name or digest setting and then uses the back link loses that edit with no warning.

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above." The #invite-sent section displays no email address itself; the address was entered on the preceding #invite-member screen.
findings.fix: Repeat the entered email address on the invite-sent confirmation itself, rather than referring back to it.
findings.violation: The confirmation refers to the address "entered above" without repeating it, but "above" is not meaningful on what the artifact treats as a separate state from the one where the address was entered, so the user cannot verify which address the invite went to without navigating back to check.
